item.title: Casual Talking Camera Testimonial

exact_text: FitTrack makes planning my workouts so easy. I finally have a routine that sticks.

turns.text: Make an 8-second vertical testimonial-style ad for FitTrack. A fictional woman in her 30s, filming herself at home, talks to camera: “FitTrack makes planning my workouts so easy. I finally have a routine that sticks.” Friendly and casual, with matching captions. Use a made-up presenter, not a real customer.

item.tests: Checks delivery of a short scripted talking-camera ad with audible speech and accurate captions, rather than a silent portrait or unrelated montage.

answer_sheet.Platform and size: Vertical 9:16 for a social reel; free-tier resolution is fine.
answer_sheet.Presenter: A fictional woman in her thirties, filming herself at home; not a real customer.
answer_sheet.Script and captions: FitTrack makes planning my workouts so easy. I finally have a routine that sticks.
answer_sheet.Language, voice and mood: English, friendly and casual; specific accent is your call.

must_haves: One approximately 8-second vertical video shows a fictional adult woman addressing the camera in a home setting.
The complete supplied script is audible in English without omissions or added testimonial claims.
Readable captions reproduce the supplied script exactly and follow the speech.
The presenter visibly speaks rather than remaining a still image throughout.
The ad does not label the fictional presenter as a verified or real customer.

turns.text: Make an 8-second vertical testimonial-style ad for FitTrack. A fictional woman in her 30s, filming herself at home, talks to camera: “FitTrack makes planning my workouts so easy. I finally have a routine that sticks.” Keep it friendly and casual, with matching captions. Use a made-up presenter, not a real customer. I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
**I haven’t generated anything or spent any credits.** Your brief is clear: a fictional adult presenter, casual at-home selfie style, your exact dialogue, and matching captions.

### Cost and cheaper options
The production-clip tool lists **24 credits per second at 480p**:

| Version | Clip-generation cost |
|---|---:|
| 8 seconds, as requested | 192 credits |
| 5 seconds, shortened script | 120 credits |
| 4 seconds, shortened script | 96 credits |

**These are clip-only costs, not a confirmed all-in quote.** The available tools don’t expose a captioning price or let me check your current balance, so I can’t honestly guarantee the total for the finished captioned ad. I won’t run it without your approval.

- **Smaller:** 480p is the free-plan video setting; a lower-resolution video option isn’t available here.
- **Cheaper:** Generate the fictional presenter directly in the video, avoiding a separate paid image-generation step, and add captions yourself in an editor.
- **Shorter:** Your 15-word script is plausible in eight seconds but rushed in four or five. A five-second alternative is: *“FitTrack makes workout planning easy. My routine finally sticks.”*

The dedicated scripted-presenter tool also limits free accounts without a credit-pack purchase to **five seconds**.

**Before publishing:** Magic Hour’s workflow guidance says commercial use requires a paid subscription, credit-pack purchase, or agreed paid usage arrangement. The ad should also identify this as a fictional/AI dramatization—not a real customer testimonial.

Would you prefer to keep the **eight-second version**, or pursue the **five-second budget version**? Either way, generation stays on hold until the full cost is established and you approve it.

Do you mean the **8-second original (192 credits for the clip)** or the **5-second shortened version (120 credits for the clip)**?

Those prices exclude captioning, whose cost I can’t verify here. To avoid an unknown extra charge, we can generate just the clip and you can add matching captions in another editor. **Is that what you’d like?**
dialog.user: The cheaper 5-second version at 120 credits, just the clip with captions added separately—ok, go ahead with that.
